title: Az ábécé és a hangok
summary: Hungarian is spelled the way it sounds. Learn the few letters that differ from English and you can read any word aloud.

sections.text: Hungarian spelling is very regular: **one letter = one sound**, and every letter is pronounced. The stress is always on the **first syllable** of a word.
The most common mistake: reading **s** as English s. In Hungarian **s = sh** and **sz = s**. So *busz* sounds like “boos” and *saláta* like “shalata”.
Letters made of two or three characters

**cs, dz, gy, ly, ny, sz, ty, zs** are *kétjegyű mássalhangzók* (two-character consonants). **dzs** is the only *háromjegyű mássalhangzó* (three-character consonant). Each one counts as **a single letter** in the alphabet and in dictionaries.
**q, w, x, y** only appear in foreign words and names: *IQ, whisky, xilofon*. The letter y is called *ipszilon*.
